settings.title: Settings
settings.ui_scale_setup_desc: Check the live preview and choose the scale that feels best on this screen. You can change it later in Settings.
settings.autoplay_preview_label: Play the output as soon as a render finishes
settings.autoplay_preview_hint: When off, a finished render no longer starts playing on its own — useful when batch-generating segments.
settings.appearance_help: These controls used to live in the bottom logs bar — moved here so the footer can stay focused on logs. Changes apply instantly and persist across launches.
settings.llmp_desc: Powers Cinematic & Autofit translation — the LLM rewrites each line to fit its segment's time budget so the video timing holds. Keys are stored encrypted; local providers (Ollama/LM Studio) stay fully offline.
settings.llmp_catalogue_note: The provider marked active is what answers whenever the LLM engine family is set to OpenAI-compatible in the catalogue.
settings.llmp_catalogue_link: Open the LLM family in the catalogue
settings.llmp_provider_hint: Pick a provider to configure. The active one is used for Cinematic/Autofit translation. Local providers need no key but require their server to be running.
settings.llmp_key_env: set via environment (.env) — overrides this field
settings.llmp_saved_not_active: Saved — not yet used for translation. Click “Save & use for translation” to switch.
settings.llmp_setup_hint: Choose a provider, start its server or add its API key, then connect. Sado verifies a model response before enabling LLM features.
settings.llmp_err_config: Complete the provider settings: Base URL, model, and any required API key or account ID.
settings.llmp_err_auth: Key rejected (401/403) — check your API key.
settings.llmp_err_not_found: Not found (404) — check the model name and Base URL path.
settings.llmp_err_rate_limit: Rate-limited (429) — the key works; try again in a moment.
settings.llmp_err_network: Can't reach the provider — check the Base URL, your network, or that the local server is running.
settings.llmp_env_override: set via an environment variable — overrides this field
settings.llmp_active_env_pin: LLM selection is pinned by LLM_DEFAULT_PROVIDER or OMNIVOICE_LLM_BACKEND.
settings.llmp_models_truncated: first {{count}} shown — type to narrow the model name
settings.llmskills_desc: Route each AI-powered feature to its own LLM — keep sensitive work on a local model (Ollama/LM Studio) while heavier jobs use a remote provider — or switch a feature off entirely. Off behaves exactly like having no LLM configured: the feature falls back to its non-LLM path.
settings.llmskills_dub_translation_desc: Translates dub lines directly with your configured LLM provider (the Dubbing tab's 'LLM' engine). Off: the LLM engine is unavailable — pick another engine.
settings.llmskills_cinematic_translation_desc: Rewrites each translated line for natural, in-character delivery (and Autofit's time budget). Off: dubs use the Fast translation result.
settings.llmskills_slot_fitting_desc: Trims or expands a translated line so its reading time fits the segment's time slot. Off: the line is used as-is.
settings.llmskills_glossary_extract_desc: Proposes project glossary terms (names, places, recurring terminology) from the source segments. Off: add glossary terms manually.
settings.llmskills_direction_parse_desc: Turns a natural-language delivery note ("more urgent, surprised") into structured voice-direction tokens. Off: a fast keyword heuristic is used instead.
settings.llmskills_dictation_refinement_desc: Cleans final dictation transcripts — filler words, self-corrections, punctuation. Off: the raw transcript passes through unchanged.
settings.proxy_desc: HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy for downloads (video downloads, Hugging Face). Supports http://, https://, socks5://. Applies to new downloads immediately.
settings.proxy_saved: Proxy set — new downloads will use it
settings.remote_backend_desc: Run inference on another machine; leave the URL empty for the local backend. Saving reloads the app to apply.
settings.remote_backend_hint: Start the backend on the other machine with <1>OMNIVOICE_API_KEY</1> set, reach it over your tailnet, and point this app at it.
settings.remote_backend_key_placeholder: value of OMNIVOICE_API_KEY on the server
settings.remote_backend_invalid_url: Enter a valid URL starting with http:// or https:// (e.g. http://gpu-box:3900).
settings.remote_backend_confirm_unverified: This backend URL hasn't passed a connection test. Save it and reload anyway? If it's wrong, the app can't reach any backend until you change it back here.
settings.remote_backend_recovery_hint: You can change the remote backend later in Settings → Sharing.
settings.remote_backend_error_tls: The secure connection could not be verified. Check the certificate and use the Sado HTTP API port.
settings.remote_backend_error_cors: The remote backend blocked this app. Allow this app's origin in the backend CORS settings.
settings.remote_backend_error_network: The remote backend could not be reached. Check its address, network, and firewall.
settings.remote_backend_error_timeout: The remote backend did not respond in time.
settings.remote_backend_error_wrong_port: This does not look like the Sado HTTP API. Port 7443 is usually the remote-worker control port; try port 3900.
settings.ffmpeg_desc: Set a custom ffmpeg path if auto-detection fails.
settings.ffmpeg_saved: FFmpeg path set — restart backend to apply.
settings.audio_tools_desc: The media engine (FFmpeg, FFprobe) and video downloader (yt-dlp) the app manages for you.
settings.audio_tools_manual_hint: Prefer your package manager? Install FFmpeg yourself (macOS: brew install ffmpeg · Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install ffmpeg · Windows: winget install ffmpeg) and press Use system copy. Nothing is ever installed system-wide by the app.
settings.audio_tools_ffmpeg_desc: Converts, dubs, and mixes audio/video. The app resolves it automatically — override only if you need a specific build.
settings.audio_tools_ffprobe_desc: Reads media metadata (durations, frame rates) for Smart Fit and imports.
settings.audio_tools_ytdlp_desc: Powers video/clip imports. Site support changes faster than app releases — update it here when imports start failing.
settings.audio_tools_ytdlp_updated: yt-dlp {{version}} installed — restart the backend to apply.
settings.audio_tools_ytdlp_restored: Tested yt-dlp restored — restart the backend to apply.
settings.audio_tools_moved_note: The FFmpeg override moved to its own panel with more control (version, origin, restore).
settings.diagnostics_copied: Diagnostics copied — paste into your issue report.
settings.updater_desktop: Updater only runs in the desktop app.
settings.clear_frontend_confirm: Clear the in-memory frontend log buffer?
settings.clear_tauri_confirm: Truncate the Tauri-side log files? The OS will continue to write new entries.
settings.nothing_to_clear: Nothing to clear — no Tauri log file on disk yet.
settings.clear_backend_confirm: Clear the backend runtime + crash logs? This cannot be undone.
settings.reset_longform_failed: Sado couldn’t safely clear saved projects. Your project data was left intact; free some storage or restart the app, then try again.
settings.hf_token_also_clear: Also clear saved HuggingFace CLI token files
settings.hf_token_desc: Resolved across three sources in priority order — App, Env, HF CLI.
settings.hf_source_app_help: Stored encrypted in Sado's local SQLite store. Set or clear here.
settings.hf_source_env_help: Set via HF_TOKEN in your shell. Read-only from the UI.
settings.hf_source_cli_help: Written by `huggingface-cli login`. Read-only from the UI.
settings.mcp_desc: Give each MCP agent its own voice — bind the client id an agent sends to a voice profile.
settings.mcp_hint: Agents reach Sado at /mcp and identify themselves with a client id (e.g. claude-code). Bind that id to a voice so the agent always speaks in that profile.
settings.mcp_empty: No bindings yet — add an agent's client id below.
settings.credentials_desc: API keys and tokens, set for this session.
settings.usage_desc: What you have made with Sado — counted on your own machine.
settings.usage_privacy: These numbers are counted from your own history, on this machine, and are never sent anywhere. Sado has no analytics service — nothing here leaves your computer.
settings.usage_empty: You haven't generated anything yet — make something and it'll show up here.
settings.network_desc: Proxy for downloads and model fetches.
settings.translation_desc: How dubbing translates dialogue, and which engine does it.
settings.translate_quality_desc: Fast is literal and quick; Cinematic uses the LLM for natural phrasing.
settings.translation_providers_desc: API keys for the DeepL and Microsoft online translators. Saved and restored across restarts.
settings.translation_llm_desc: Cinematic and Autofit translation use a high-quality LLM.
settings.translation_llm_row_desc: Choose, test, and activate a provider (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, a local Ollama, …) in LLM Providers. Keys are stored encrypted; local providers stay fully offline.
settings.review_mode_desc: Pause between pipeline stages so you can review ASR / translation output.
settings.header_live_stats: Show live system metrics in header
settings.header_live_stats_desc: Adds a live RAM / CPU / VRAM monitor to the top bar (off by default).
settings.nav_style_desc: Switch workspaces from an icon rail down the window edge, or from tabs across the title bar.
settings.storage_desc: Where Sado keeps your data and outputs.
settings.uninstall_desc: Delete everything Sado has written to this machine, then quit.
settings.uninstall_body: Sado is fully local, so uninstalling is just deleting the folders it wrote. This removes your voice profiles, projects, and generated audio permanently — there is no undo. Removing the app itself is a separate step.
settings.uninstall_target_models: Downloaded model weights (shared Hugging Face cache)
settings.uninstall_confirm_body: Your voice profiles, projects, and generated audio will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.
settings.uninstall_models_caveat: The standard Hugging Face cache, shared with other AI tools on this machine — removing it may delete models Sado never downloaded. Anything Sado needs downloads again.
settings.uninstall_models_warning: This includes the shared Hugging Face cache ({{size}}) — models other AI tools downloaded may go with it.
settings.reset_desc: Put part — or all — of Sado back to how it shipped.
settings.reset_body_web: Clears locally-saved preferences (theme, language, dub settings) and reloads. Your voices, projects and generated audio are not affected.
settings.reset_tier_ui_hint: Theme, layout and dub knobs go back to defaults. Nothing on disk changes.
settings.reset_tier_settings_hint: Every preference, in the app and on disk. Your voices, projects and models are untouched.
settings.reset_tier_assets_hint: Model weights, sidecar engines, audio tools and caches. Everything you made stays. They re-download when next needed.
settings.reset_tier_everything_hint: Back to a fresh install: settings, voices, projects, audio, models, engines, logs. The app restarts on the first-run screen.
settings.reset_scope_ui_prefs: UI preferences — theme, language, layout, dub settings
settings.reset_scope_settings: App settings — engine choices, voice defaults, saved options
settings.reset_scope_history: Generation & dub history, with their audio
settings.reset_scope_content: Voices, projects, generated audio, and the app database
settings.reset_models_shared: Shared Hugging Face cache — may hold models other AI tools downloaded.
settings.reset_models_shared_warning: The model cache is the standard Hugging Face cache, shared with other AI tools on this machine — removing it may delete models Sado never downloaded. Everything Sado needs will download again on next use.
settings.reset_irreversible: Your voice profiles, projects and generated audio will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.
settings.reset_restart_note: Sado will restart its engine to finish. This takes a few seconds.
settings.reset_partial: Some items could not be removed: {{paths}}
settings.storage_usage_desc: What Sado stores on this machine, and how much space is left.
settings.storage_manage_models_hint: Reclaim space by removing models in the Model Store
settings.storage_clear_logs_hint: Truncate the backend runtime and crash logs
settings.storage_warn_critical: Critically low disk space: {{free}} GB free on {{path}} — Sado needs at least {{min}} GB. Generation and model downloads may fail.
settings.storage_warn_low: Low disk space: {{free}} GB free on {{path}} — getting close to the {{min}} GB minimum.
settings.storage_warn_unreadable: Could not fully scan {{path}} — the size shown may be incomplete.
settings.history_retention_desc: How many takes to keep before the oldest are cleaned up.
settings.history_retention_help: After each generation, the oldest unstarred takes over this limit are removed along with their audio files. Starred takes are always kept. Set 0 to keep everything.
settings.history_retention_cap_hint: Starred takes never count against cleanup · 0 = unlimited
settings.perf_torch_compile_na: Windows only — not needed on this platform
settings.perf_torch_compile_note: Uses eager execution to avoid Triton memory errors.
settings.perf_torch_compile_hint: Uses eager execution to avoid Triton memory errors. <issueLink>#65</issueLink> · <crashLink>#2135</crashLink>
settings.generate_budget_desc: How long one generation may run before it is abandoned as too heavy for this hardware. CPU renders are legitimately slower than accelerated ones, so they get their own, higher floor.
settings.generate_timeout_gpu_note: Used when generation runs on CUDA, ROCm, MPS, or another accelerator. Also used for CPU-family generation if no CPU budget below is set.
settings.generate_timeout_cpu_note: Used when generation runs on the CPU. Once saved here, this always governs CPU-family generation — independent of the accelerated budget above.
settings.generate_timeout_invalid: Enter a number of seconds greater than 0 and at most {{max}}.
settings.generate_timeout_saved: Saved. Restart Sado for the new budget to take effect.
settings.storage_clear_temp_hint: Delete Sado's own files in the temp directory
settings.storage_clear_temp_confirm: Delete Sado's temporary working files? Don't do this while a dub or batch job is running.
settings.history_retention_load_failed: Could not load the current retention limit
settings.workers_desc: Send individual jobs to GPUs on your other machines. Results come back here. Nothing is sent until you add a worker and approve it.
settings.workers_enable_hint: While this is off, no connection is accepted and nothing leaves this machine.
settings.workers_port_conflict: Remote workers are unavailable because another Sado instance is already accepting them on this port. Close the other instance, or set OMNIVOICE_WORKER_PORT to a different port and restart Sado.
settings.workers_endpoint_hint: A worker has to be able to reach this address. On different networks, a VPN such as Tailscale is the reliable way.
settings.workers_add_hint: Generate a token, then paste it into OmniVoice on the other machine.
settings.workers_token_once: Copy this now — it is shown only once, works only once, and expires in 15 minutes.
settings.workers_none: No workers yet. Generate a token to add your first one.
settings.workers_remove_confirm: Remove {{name}}? Its key is revoked, so it cannot reconnect without a new token.
settings.inbound_revoke_confirm: Remove access for {{label}}? Their connection string stops working immediately. Everyone else stays connected.
settings.inbound_desc: Let other machines connect to this one so several people can share its GPU. Every connection is encrypted and pinned to this machine’s certificate.
settings.inbound_enable_hint: Other people connect to this machine instead of it connecting to them. Nobody gets in without a connection string you create.
settings.inbound_bind_exposed: Anyone who can reach {{address}} can connect with a valid connection string. TLS encrypts the session and pins this machine’s certificate; keep each string private and remove access when it is no longer needed.
settings.inbound_bind_local: Only this machine can reach it. Enter your network address to let other machines connect.
settings.inbound_add_person_hint: Creates a connection string for one person. Give each person their own, so removing one does not disconnect everybody.
settings.inbound_shown_once: Copy this now — it is not shown again. Give it only to {{label}}.
settings.inbound_shown_once_warning: Treat it like a password and send it privately. Its certificate fingerprint pins the encrypted connection to this GPU machine.
settings.inbound_connect_desc: Paste the connection string someone gave you. The machine has to be accepting connections for this to work.
settings.inbound_connect_hint: Starts with ovnode:// and includes the key, address, port and certificate fingerprint.
settings.inbound_request_failed: Could not reach that GPU machine. Check that it is online and accepting connections, then try again.
settings.models_dir_help: Where model weights are stored. Choose a larger or faster drive when needed; changes apply after restart.
settings.models_dir_saved: Models directory saved — restart to apply
settings.models_dir_reverted: Default directory restored — restart to apply
settings.models_dir_reset_hint: Revert to the default cache location
settings.models_dir_restart: ↻ Restart Sado to use the new location.
settings.worker_join_code_hint: Single-use and expires in 15 minutes. Generate it on the machine that will send the work.
settings.worker_join_desc: Let another copy of Sado send jobs to this machine. Paste the join code it showed you — or scan its QR with your phone and paste it here.
settings.worker_join_env: OMNIVOICE_WORKER_MODE is set in this machine’s environment, so it decides — change it there.
settings.worker_join_ok: Ulandi. Bu kompyuter endi ish qabul qiladi.
settings.workers_add_hint_qr: Generate a token, then scan the QR from the other machine or paste the code into its Remote workers settings.
settings.workers_qr_alt: QR code carrying this code — scan it from the other machine
settings.workers_step_1: Install Sado on the machine with the GPU.
settings.workers_step_3: Scan the QR there, or paste the code into its Remote workers settings.
settings.workers_token_qr_hint: On the other machine: Settings → System → Remote workers → Join, then scan or paste.
settings.compute_device_desc: Which device the backend runs models on. Auto is right for almost everyone.
settings.compute_device_env_pinned: Pinned by the OMNIVOICE_DEVICE environment variable
settings.compute_device_ignored: That device was not detected on this machine — Auto is in effect
settings.compute_device_restart: Takes effect after the app restarts
settings.compute_device_note: Only devices detected on this machine are listed. CPU always works; pinning a device never invents hardware.
settings.generate_timeout_shadowed_note: An environment variable outside Sado (shell, .env file, or container) is currently setting this — your saved value here is ignored until that variable is removed.
settings.generate_timeout_shadowed_toast: Saved, but an environment variable outside Sado is currently setting this — it will keep being used until that variable is removed.

dub.auto_glossary_title: One extra LLM pass reads the whole transcript and extracts the video's theme plus key terms, so names and terminology stay consistent across segments. Your manual glossary entries always win.

Quit the other instance and relaunch; if nothing is visibly running, an orphaned backend from a previous session is still holding the port.
errors.crash_oom_kill: It was force-killed (signal 9), which usually means the operating system ran out of memory (RAM) and stopped it. Close memory-heavy apps, pick a smaller ASR model in Settings → Models, or flush the TTS model before transcribing.
errors.crash_native_fault: It crashed inside the compute stack rather than running out of memory — that points at a GPU driver that does not match the bundled CUDA runtime, or a model file that downloaded incompletely. Update your GPU driver, then re-download the model from Settings → Models (it repairs a partial download in place). If it keeps happening, switch to a crash-isolated engine in Settings → Engines — "Sado (subprocess)" for synthesis, "Faster-Whisper (crash-isolated subprocess)" for transcription. Those run the model in a separate process, so a crash like this takes down that process instead of the whole backend.
errors.report_failed: Couldn't open the bug report. Please try again, or copy the details above into a new issue.
errors.backend_shutting_down: Sado is shutting down. Reopen the app and try again.
errors.crash_broken_env: It died while loading its own Python dependencies, so this is not about memory or your GPU — the environment is incomplete or was left half-updated. Use "Clean & Retry" in Settings → Logs → Backend, which rebuilds it from scratch; that repairs it in place, without touching your voices or projects. If it still fails afterwards, the crash details name the exact package that would not import.
errors.crash_vram_default: On smaller GPUs the usual cause is running out of VRAM while loading the ASR model on top of the TTS model: flush the TTS model first, or pick a smaller ASR model in the engine's Weights list in Model Catalogue.
errors.stream_cut_backend_alive: The stream ended early, but the backend is still running — so it did not crash. In a served or containerised setup this is usually a reverse proxy or load balancer buffering or timing out the connection: disable response buffering for this route (nginx: proxy_buffering off; X-Accel-Buffering: no) and raise its read timeout. Running the desktop app directly, or on localhost without a proxy, will confirm it.
errors.stream_cut_backend_alive_local: The stream ended early, but the backend is still running — so it did not crash. The app lost its connection to the backend mid-job; that happens when a long step goes quiet for minutes, and the backend usually finishes the job anyway. Give it a few minutes and reopen the job from its history, or check the backend log (Settings → Logs → Backend) for what it was doing.

crash.notice: The voice backend crashed ({{exit}}) {{ago}} ago and is being restarted automatically.
crash.details_intro: The backend process died unexpectedly ({{exit}}) {{ago}} ago. The error output it left behind is below — reporting it helps us fix the crash.
crash.notice_unclean: The previous session ended without a clean shutdown {{ago}} ago. This is often harmless — the machine slept, the app was force-quit, or a VM/container stopped.
crash.details_intro_unclean: The previous run's shutdown marker was never cleared, {{ago}} ago. Sado cannot tell whether it crashed or was simply interrupted — sleeping, force-quitting, or stopping a VM/container leaves the same trace. If everything works now, nothing needs doing.

backend_start_failure.notice: Sado's backend couldn't start — nothing can run until it does.
backend_start_failure.title: The backend couldn't start
backend_start_failure.intro: The app captured this while trying to start the backend. Including this output in a report helps us fix it.
backend_start_failure.retry_hint: Try "Retry" in Settings → Logs → Backend. If it fails again, "Clean & Retry" rebuilds the environment from scratch.

backendUnreachable.contact_recent: It was answering {{ago}} ago and then stopped responding, and no crash was recorded — so it may still be alive but wedged on a heavy job that is holding the engine.
backendUnreachable.contact_never: It has not answered at all this session — it may never have started.
backendUnreachable.dev: Can't reach the local Sado backend. {{contact}} In `bun run dev` the backend runs with auto-reload, so any file change — including a save while a request was in flight — restarts it and drops the connection. Retry the action first; if it was a reload, it just works. If it keeps failing, check the terminal running `bun run dev` for a Python traceback or an exit banner, and omnivoice.log in your Sado data folder for the last thing the backend logged.
backendUnreachable.server: Can't reach the Sado backend server. {{contact}} Check the server logs for the cause (e.g. `docker logs <container>` or `journalctl`) — and note that if Docker serves this page, the page itself can go down with the backend.
backendUnreachable.misrouted: The server answering {{url}} is not a Sado backend — it returned its own 404 page. API requests are landing on the wrong host: check the Backend URL in Settings → Sharing, or, if a reverse proxy serves this UI, its route for API paths.
backendUnreachable.desktop: Can't reach the local Sado backend. {{contact}} Open the crash notice if one appeared, or Settings → Logs → Backend for the last thing it logged — "{{retry}}" restarts it, and "{{cleanRetry}}" rebuilds its environment if it will not come back.
